Right: without the edge X-C, drawn dashed in the accent color, C misses part of the clique; the graph is still split but is_complete_split_graph() returns False." width="100%"} A *complete split graph* is a split graph with every possible edge between its two parts: a clique whose nodes are joined to everything, and an independent set whose nodes are joined to the whole clique and to nothing else. Stars (a one-node clique) and complete graphs (an empty independent set) are the extremes. Its nodes therefore take only two roles, a core that reaches everyone and a periphery that reaches only the core, as in a hub-and-spoke network with fully connected hubs. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is a complete split graph. The empty graph, a single node and any graph with no edges (an empty clique) are. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~is_split_graph`) : Split, with any edges between the clique and the independent set. ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Every clique node is joined to all other nodes, and an independent-set node has a non-neighbor unless it is the only one. So the graph is complete split exactly when the nodes with fewer than $n - 1$ neighbors form an independent set, which is checked in $O(V + E)$ time. Results match NetworkX pull request #8126's `is_complete_split_graph`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two hubs joined to each other and to three spokes form a complete split graph. Dropping one hub-spoke edge leaves a split graph that is no longer complete: ::: {#17e73dcb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["hub1", "hub2", "a", "b", "c"]) g.add_edges([("hub1", "hub2")]) g.add_edges([(h, s) for h in ("hub1", "hub2") for s in ("a", "b", "c")]) before = g.is_complete_split_graph() g.delete_edge("hub1", "c") before, g.is_complete_split_graph(), g.is_split_graph() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False, True) ``` ::: :::
